composite_primary_key.citation: linkml-model slot 'identifier' Comments ('There can be at most one identifier or key per container') plus slot 'unique_keys' (compound unique_key_slots)
composite_primary_key.rationale: A class may declare exactly one 'identifier' or 'key' slot — never more than one, and never a compound identifier. A true multi-column IDENTITY (e.g. OUTCOME_RULE on (task_version_id, sequence_no) as the row's identifying key) cannot be expressed as a compound `identifier`. The documented alternative, `unique_keys`, gives compound UNIQUENESS but is explicitly not identity ('key: true is not merely syntactic sugar for a unique_keys definition' — key/identifier slots get special treatment such as dict-inlining that unique_keys does not). So a composite primary key is representable only as a compound unique_keys constraint standing in for the PK, which is a workaround relative to what the source model actually needs (an identifying composite key), not a native composite-identifier construct.

json_payload_column.citation: docs/schemas/advanced.html 'Any' type (linkml:Any) section; absence of a documented opaque JSON scalar type among linkml-model builtin types (only Jsonpath/Jsonpointer string-pattern types were found)
json_payload_column.rationale: LinkML has no native opaque-JSON scalar comparable to a database JSONB/JSON column. The two documented escape hatches are (a) `range: Any` (linkml:Any), which permits any typed object but is meant for polymorphic typed values, not an intentionally-untyped blob, or (b) `range: string`, which stores the JSON as an opaque string with no schema-level structure at all. Neither is a first-class 'this column holds arbitrary JSON' construct; both require the schema author to step outside LinkML's typed-slot model.

enumerated_string_domain.rationale: Directly and natively supported: an `enums:` block with `permissible_values:` restricts a slot's range to a fixed value set, exactly matching FOLDER_RUN.execution_context (SCHEDULED|MANUAL) and NAMED_RESOURCE_LINK.link_kind (HOST_CAPACITY|NAMED_RESOURCE).

multiple_self_referencing_fks_one_table.citation: SlotDefinition.range general mechanism (linkml-model) — no documented cardinality restriction on how many slots of a class may take that same class as their range
multiple_self_referencing_fks_one_table.rationale: A slot's `range` can name any class, including the class the slot itself belongs to. Nothing in the documentation restricts a class to at most one self-referencing slot, so origin_instance_id, cyclic_root_instance_id, and previous_iteration_id can each be declared as ordinary slots with range: TaskInstance. No dedicated 'self-reference' language feature exists or is needed — this follows from the general range mechanism, not from a documented example specific to multiple simultaneous self-references, so the citation is inferential rather than a worked LinkML example.

nullable_foreign_key.citation: linkml-model slot 'required', Description ('true means that the slot must be present')
nullable_foreign_key.rationale: Slots are optional (nullable) unless `required: true` is set; this is the documented default. A class-range slot such as TASK_INSTANCE.folder_run_id or .plan_id left without `required: true` is a nullable foreign key by default LinkML behavior.

multi_column_unique_not_pk.citation: linkml-model slot 'unique_keys' and docs/schemas/constraints.html compound-key YAML example
multi_column_unique_not_pk.rationale: unique_keys with a list of unique_key_slots is precisely a multi-column UNIQUE constraint independent of the class's identifier/key slot, matching PLAN (domain_id, odate) and NAMED_RESOURCE (domain_id, name).

one_to_zero_or_one.citation: linkml-model slot 'required' (default false) combined with SlotDefinition.multivalued (default false)
one_to_zero_or_one.rationale: A class-range slot that is neither required nor multivalued is a singular optional (zero-or-one) reference, which is the standard LinkML default for any non-required, non-multivalued slot with a class range — matching ATTEMPT ||--o| ATTEMPT_RESULT.

value_constraint_beyond_type.citation: docs/schemas/advanced.html, any_of / equals_string boolean range-expression section
value_constraint_beyond_type.rationale: `any_of` combined with `equals_string` (or a numeric range expression with minimum_value) lets a slot be declared as 'range: integer with minimum_value 1' OR 'equals_string: ALL', directly matching resource_task_weight's 'decimal positive integer OR literal ALL' requirement. The documentation itself flags these boolean/rules features as experimental with behavior 'not guaranteed to stay consistent', which is recorded as a limitation on how solid this classification is going forward.

several_logical_schemas_in_one_database.citation: docs/generators/sqltable.html mapping-algorithm statement 'Each schema S corresponds to one database schema D'
several_logical_schemas_in_one_database.rationale: The SQL DDL generator's documented algorithm maps one LinkML schema file to exactly one database schema. No documented option was found (see contrary-evidence record) for tagging individual classes with a target database-schema name so that one LinkML source produces tables split across configuration/runtime/audit/resources schemas in one physical database. The closest workaround is authoring four separate LinkML schema files (using `imports` to share common types) and running gen-sqlddl once per file, then hand-assembling the four DDL outputs against one database — which requires manual assembly outside any single documented command.

cross_cutting_convention_domain_id.rationale: Mixins let a schema author compose a shared slot (e.g. a DomainScoped mixin carrying domain_id) into every class that needs it, but this is a schema-AUTHORING convention, not an automatically-verified constraint: nothing in the mixins documentation states that a linter or validator checks, after the fact, that every class in some group actually uses the mixin. Enforcing 'domain_id present on every Domain-owned table' as a checked invariant — rather than a convention the author must remember to apply — is not shown as a mixins capability in this documentation; see the tooling record for whether linkml-lint's rule set covers this (it does not, per its documented eight built-in rules).
